summary:
The kotlin port is sound in what it declares: every fact I opened against the runtime holds. The porter's numbers reproduce exactly, and the only thing failing the one command is the callcheck reader gap the porter named. Four fixes are needed before its pages count as evidence.

**Reproduced.**
- `REGEN=1 tools/portcheck.sh sdkgen out kotlin`: exit 1. Every number is identical to the porter's final.log; the only failure is callcheck's 6 ARITY findings.
- `SCRATCH=1`: identical to the porter's scratch2.log (OPEN 24/4/92 ledger, 23/21/11 blocks, NOT JUDGED `named`, UNATTESTED `ref.noun`, 29 ABSENT).
- Guard 4/4; guard+reader 81/81; build exit 0 with the tree clean.
- Suite: 2635 tests, 2630 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.
- Golden 2/2, with 0 non-kotlin golden lines changed.
- Line counts: 753 deleted against 220 added (3.42x), 262 with the forms (2.87x).
- sharewords: only-kotlin 4.0% and the note 4.0% of 58,511 words.
- No other language's page changed outside the kotlin quick start.
- Commits carry no trailer and name no tool.

**The callcheck gap is real, and wider than reported.** callcheck's argsAt splits `mutableMapOf<String, Any?>(...)` on the comma inside the type arguments. That gives the 6 false ARITY findings, and the reverse too:
- a call that really drops `ctrl` inside a typed map reads as 2 arguments and passes (attacks f11 and p04);
- `list(null)` also passes, because a local `val list` in Struct.kt:434 is read as a list overload with no parameters (p05).

The porter's patched copy fixes the first and not the second.

**Found by compiling, not by any tool.**
- I compiled the four review variations' own pages with gradle offline, which uses the Kotlin 2.2.0 compiler already in ~/.gradle; I downloaded nothing. The REFERENCE blocks got only the imports the tutorial prints.
- 91 NEW and 88 OLD blocks compile, except 4 NEW REFERENCE blocks in ref-issues (8 errors, Unresolved reference 'SdkEntity').
- Cause: the kotlin provider imports SdkEntity only when the tutorial reads a record. ref-issues' tutorial only updates, while its REFERENCE list examples cast to SdkEntity. OLD always imported SdkEntity, and rust's provider imports unconditionally for this exact reason.
- The tutorial and root quick start ran in test mode (seeded mock), OLD and NEW, for B and crud-basic: 2/2 each, records printed.

**The stream note is a shared fact written as a note.** Every runtime accepts its own signal form (java BooleanSupplier, scala Function0, swift a closure, perl a coderef, csharp a CancellationToken, js an AbortSignal, go a channel). By the guide's rule this is a fact or a recorded interface gap, not a note. It is half of kotlin's per-language words.

**What the attacks showed (34 run).**
- Every mutation of a declared value is caught by the guard, naming the fact.
- Not caught by the guard, and caught only by OPEN classes a hand record could close:
  - declaring `deleted`, which the bound type SdkEntity lacks;
  - a false note changed in both the provider and its pin;
  - removing `arity`, which reverts the tutorial to `load()`;
  - a test signature written with no receiver;
  - operation calls made on the type;
  - a dropped cast (does not compile);
  - the hook's package changed.
- Caught by nothing beyond the baseline: moving the client class's package in the template while the pages keep `import ...core.DemoSDK`.
- `prints: 'listFields'` is reported ATTESTED on the same 114 blocks that attest `record`.

H1 holds for kotlin. H3 holds. H4 holds, with one fixable regression (ref-issues).

required_fixes.change: Print `import <module>.SdkEntity` unconditionally in the tutorial and the root quick start (or whenever the page's REFERENCE casts to it), not only when `used.print || used.field`.
required_fixes.why: The REFERENCE prints no imports (shared design), and its list examples cast `(item as SdkEntity)`. In ref-issues the NEW tutorial imports only DemoSDK. Compiling the REFERENCE blocks with the tutorial's imports: NEW 8 errors (4 blocks, `Unresolved reference 'SdkEntity'`), OLD 0, because OLD always imported it. Precedent: Syntax_rust.ts:113-117 imports unconditionally for the same reason. An unused import is only a warning in Kotlin.

required_fixes.change: (1) Treat a type-argument list `<...>` after a word character as a bracket, as forms.ts bracketed() does (the porter's run/callcheck-generic.js). (2) Do not count a local variable declaration (`val list = parent as MutableList<Any?>`, Struct.kt:434,460) as an overload of a runtime member.
required_fixes.why: Today: 6 false ARITY findings block the port. The reverse is worse: `load(mutableMapOf<String, Any?>("id" to "planet_id"))` with ctrl dropped reads as 2 arguments and passes (p04, f11). `list(null)` passes because `required` becomes 0 (p05; callcheck prints "declares 2 or 0"). Measured: the patched copy gives 0 findings on the clean pages and catches the dropped-ctrl control, but still misses `list(null)`, so (2) is also needed.

required_fixes.change: Record the stream signal's accepted form as an additive interface gap: an optional fact naming the form, with one shared sentence. The note may stay until that lands, but must be reported as a gap, not as kotlin-only prose.
required_fixes.why: Guide section 2, item 4: a fact two runtimes share is a fact or an interface gap, never a note. Every runtime has a signal form: java BooleanSupplier (EntityBase.fragment.java), scala Function0 (`val aborted: () => Boolean = signal match`), swift `@Sendable () -> Bool`, perl a coderef, csharp CancellationToken, js AbortSignal, go a channel. Kotlin's note is one value of that fact. It prints under every entity: 2350 words, 4.0% of kotlin's printed words, half of its per-language prose.

required_fixes.change: Add the early-end line `if (source.hasNext() && !aborted()) source.next() else end` (EntityBase.fragment.kt:248) to the quote.
required_fixes.why: The guide asks for two quotes: the read and the early end. The citation quotes the read (:187) and the construction of `aborted` (:233). The line that ends the stream appears only in the cancel absence's excepted region. The value (true) is right.

not_caught.consequence: Guard passes: guard.ts:150-160 skips a signature whose call reads as free. On kotlin's page, a member without a receiver is how instance members are written. 1 OPEN class only.

not_caught.consequence: Guard passes: arity is checked only when declared. The tutorial reverts to `load()` and `list()`, which no kotlin call can be. Fails only on OPEN 3, STALE 2 and ABSENT 1, all hand-decidable.

not_caught.consequence: Guard passes. Only ABSENT 'Returns a copy of the current match criteria.', which an absent reason closes.

not_caught.consequence: callcheck is silent on both. The B false finding merely moves to auth-basic's identical line. Caught only as 1 OPEN block class.
Fact sheet: ATTESTED ('OLD reads as listFields in 114'), the same 114 blocks that attest `record`; the minimal pair cannot tell record from listFields. Fails only on 2 OPEN tutorial block classes.
